text:
ana: Kicked off a shadowbench for the new int8 reranker against a prod-like mix. Quick heads-up: MRR is down ~3% on short queries (<5 tokens), NDCG ~1.5% down. Not seeing the same drop on long queries.
ben: Ugh. Which slice exactly? small/short or conversational? link to the run? :eyes:
ana: short_queries slice (single-pass, top10 candidates). Uploaded logs to S3: s3://redwood-shadowbench/1719465555/int8-run.tar.gz
chloe: Could be priming/priming-length interaction with quantized weights. Did you try disabling query priming?
dinesh: Also check tokenization/prefix padding — int8 can be sensitive to slight token shifts.
ana: Good call — I ran a quick ablation: with priming removed MRR for short_queries recovered ~1.8% (so still ~1.2% below float). With priming kept but using pad_to=32 instead of pad_to=64 it recovered ~1.4%.
ben: So both priming + pad length interact. Any changes to candidate ordering or soft labels?
nana: Candidate generation identical to baseline. Soft labels unchanged. Seed 42 used. I re-ran with seed 7 and saw similar pattern (so not seed-only).
chloe: Share the eval command you ran?
nana:
```bash
python infra/eval_shadowbench.py \
  --model rerank-v2-int8 \
  --slice short_queries \
  --priming true \
  --pad_to 64 \
  --seed 42 \
  --bootstrap 1000 \
  --metrics ndcg@10 mrr
```
nana: The float baseline command is the same except --model rerank-v2-fp16.
dinesh: Can we narrow whether the issue is score calibration (rescaling) or ordering difference? Compare pairwise swaps between float vs int8 on short_queries. If order differs, it's ranking error; if order same but metric lower, likely calibration/NDCG sensitivity.
ben: I ran a quick pairwise diff; ~2.1% of pairs flip on short_queries at top5. That's correlated with the MRR drop.
nana: Interesting — I also tried applying a simple score rescale (multiply int8 scores by 1.02) and NDCG/MRR both improved ~0.6%. So part calibration.
chloe: Two hypotheses: (1) quantization noise amplifies priming tokens, shifting attention for short contexts; (2) internal softmax temperature changed due to quant rounding. Could try hybrid quant (last softmax layer fp16).
dinesh: Also try kvpack off/on — there was a small change in runtime that can affect float path vs int8 postprocessing.
nana: Plan: (A) run int8 with priming disabled (already did) and with hybrid-softmax fp16; (B) run int8 with last-N layers fp16; (C) collect pairwise swap table + per-query examples where top1 changed. I'll tag results here.
ben: Add a targeted eval on human-labeled short queries (gold set of 2k) — bootstrap CI so we know significance. If drop is outside CI we need roll-back or canary.
nana: Yep. Bootstrapped 1000 already; p-value ~0.02 for short_queries. Will run 10k bootstrap and upload outputs.
chloe: Also try re-quantizing with per-channel calibration vs per-tensor. We saw differences on passage-level tasks before.
dinesh: If hybrid-softmax fixes ordering, that's our mitigation path for bring-up. Might be acceptable for Dedicated customers.
eval-bot: shadowbench run queued: job 1719465601. Notifying when complete.
nana: Thanks — I'll post the per-query diffs + top offenders when job finishes. Action items: ana -> full hybrid runs + 10k bootstrap; ben -> assemble gold short-query 2k set and run significance test; chloe -> try per-channel re-quant and hybrid-softmax prototype.
ben: tagging @oncall if we need rollback plan for canary tomorrow. :alarm_clock: 
nana: FYI, console shows slight latency improvement on int8 (~18%) which is why we prioritized this bring-up. Need to weigh latency wins vs small relevance regression.
chloe: Agreed. If we can recover ~1.2% MRR with hybrid-softmax and per-channel re-quant, this is probably an acceptable net win.
dinesh: Thanks all — keep thread updated. Small message: include 3 example queries where top1 flips in the final artifact so product can sanity-check.
nana: Will do.
